title: The Pen and the Stars
notes: Classical commentators, among them Ibn Kathir, relate that Idris was the first to write with the pen and to sew garments; some accounts also link him with the study of the stars. These come from narrations, not the Quran, and they vary in strength.
art: Idris is shown only through hands of light and, at night, a small figure of light seen from behind; the writing is flowing marks, not words.
imagePrompt: Daylight inside a simple workroom of stone blocks, a single golden beam of sunlight falling through a small window across a timber table full of floating dust, sheets of parchment, an ink pot and reed pens; a close-up of soft hands of light dipping a reed pen and drawing the first flowing lines on the parchment, the strokes spilling off the page and spreading across the whole frame into the parchment texture of the story; then hands of light stitching two pieces of linen into a garment; then a flat rooftop at night under a deep indigo sky, a small figure of light pointing upward as silver ink lines join the brightest stars into patterns; warm gold to indigo and silver, no faces.

beats.say: In a simple room of stone, a beam of morning light fell across the table.
Many scholars related that Idris was among the first to write with the pen.
Tradition also remembers him sewing garments and watching the stars.
